sanskrit: tvayā pūrvam ātharvāṇo jaghnū rakṣāṃsy oṣadhe | tvayā jaghāna kaśyapas tvayā kṛṇvo agastyaḥ ||
english: By thee, O herb, the Ātharvaṇas first smote the demons; by thee Kaśyapa smote them, by thee did Agastya destroy them.

sanskrit: tvayā vayam apsaraso gandharvāṃś cātayāmasi | ajaśṛṅgy aja rakṣaḥ sarvān gandhena nāśaya ||
english: By thee we drive away the Apsarasas and the Gandharvas. O Ajaśṛṅgī, by thy fragrance destroy all demons.

sanskrit: nadīṃ yantv apsaraso apāntāram iva śvasan | gulgulū pīlā nalady aukṣagandhiḥ pramandinī ||
english: Let the Apsarasas go to the river, breathing as if into a wilderness — Gulgulū, Pīlā, Naladī, Aukṣagandhī, Pramandinī.

sanskrit: yatrāmartyā apsv antaḥ samudre turūr nīlī turvaśī puṇḍarīkā | tat paretā apsarasaḥ pratibuddhā abhūtana ||
english: Where the immortal ones dwell within the waters of the ocean — Turū, Nīlī, Turvaśī, Puṇḍarīkā — thither go, O Apsarasas; ye have been recognized.

sanskrit: yatra preṅkho gandharvāṇāṃ divi baddho hiraṇyayaḥ | (…) ||
english: Where the golden swing of the Gandharvas is bound in the sky — [remainder lost].

sanskrit: gandharvāṇām apsarasām ānartam iti saṅgamam | (…) ||
english: The assembly-place of the Gandharvas and Apsarasas called Ānarta — [remainder lost].

sanskrit: yatrāśvatthā nyagrodhā mahārukmāḥ śikhaṇḍinaḥ | (…) ||
english: Where the aśvattha trees and the nyagrodhas, laden with great golden ornaments, stand crested — [remainder lost].

sanskrit: yatra vo 'kṣā haritā arjunā āghāṭāḥ kakaryaḥ saṃvadanti | tat paretā apsarasaḥ pratibuddhā abhūtana ||
english: Where your dice — green, white, tawny, kakara — sound together: thither go, O Apsarasas; ye have been recognized.

sanskrit: iyaṃ vīrucchikhaṇḍino gandharvasyāpsarāpateḥ | bhinattu muṣkāv api yātu śephaḥ ||
english: This creeper of Śikhaṇḍin, lord of the Gandharvas, master of the Apsarasas — may it split his testicles; may his phallus also depart.

sanskrit: eyam agann oṣadhir vīrudhāṃ vīryāvatī | ajaśṛṅgy arāṭakī tīkṣṇaśṛṅgī vy ṛṣatu ||
english: This herb has come, potent among plants — Ajaśṛṅgī, Arāṭakī with sharp horns: let it drive them away.

sanskrit: apeteto apsaraso gandharvā yatra vo gṛhāḥ | tīkṣṇaśṛṅgy arāṭaky ajaśṛṅgī vy ṛṣatu ||
english: Depart hence, O Apsarasas and Gandharvas, to where your homes are. Let Tīkṣṇaśṛṅgī, Arāṭakī, and Ajaśṛṅgī drive you away.

sanskrit: jāyā veda vo apsaraso gandharvāḥ patayo yūyam | apa krāmat puruṣād amartyā martyaṃ mā sacadhvam ||
english: The wife knows you, O Apsarasas; ye Gandharvas are the husbands. Step away from this man, O immortals; do not follow a mortal.

sanskrit: bhīmā indrasya hetayaḥ śatamṛṣṭīr ayasmai | tābhir gandharvān abhaidyān avakādān vy ṛṣatu ||
english: Fearsome are Indra's missiles, a hundred iron-tipped shafts for him. With these let it drive away the Gandharvas, the invulnerable, the Avakāda-dwellers.

sanskrit: avakādām̐ abhiśoco bhitsu dyotayamāmakān | gandharvān sarvān oṣadhe pra ṇudasva parā ṇaya ||
english: Those who dwell in the water-reeds, shining and blazing with malign heat — all the Gandharvas, O herb, push them forth, lead them away.

sanskrit: unmādayantīr abhiśocayantīr muniṃ nagnaṃ kṛṇvatīr moghahāsinam | apsaraso raghaṭo yāś caranti gandharvapatnīr ajaśṛṅgy āśaye ||
english: Those Apsarasas who roam as a swarm, maddening men, afflicting them with burning, making the sage go naked and laugh in vain, the wives of the Gandharvas — may Ajaśṛṅgī lay them low.

sanskrit: śvetīkṛṇvānaḥ puruṣaṃ viśvā rūpāṇi bobhuvat | śvevaikaṃ kapir ivaikaṃ kumāraḥ sarvakeśakaḥ | priyo dṛśe bhūtvā gandharvaḥ sacate striyaṃ tam ito nāśayāmasi ||
english: Making the man turn pale, assuming all manner of forms — like a dog at one moment, like a monkey at another, a youth with hair all about — the Gandharva, having become pleasing to look upon, follows after the woman: him from here we drive away.

sanskrit: yo vai vaśāṃ devayate pacate vāhutāmamā | mṛtyoḥ sa badhyate pāśe devānāṃ ca yamasya ca ||
english: He who sacrifices a vaśā-cow to the gods and cooks it incompletely without proper oblation — he is bound in the snare of Death, of the gods, and of Yama.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇāṃ sūryām aditiṃ vadanti vaśāṃ vācaṃ kalpayantaḥ samānīm | sapta ṛṣayo ni dadhur vācam etāṃ sarasvatī mṛḍayā kalpayantaḥ ||
english: They call the vaśā-cow the dakṣiṇā, the solar Aditi, forming her speech into a common harmony. The seven seers established this speech, Sarasvatī graciously ordering it.

sanskrit: imāṃ vaśāṃ vācam āhur vaśeti tisro vaśā atihitāḥ sadhasthe | tāsām agnau manasaikāṃ juhomi tāṃ naḥ svādvīṃ bhūtapatiḥ kṛṇotu ||
english: This vaśā they call speech itself as vaśā; three vaśās are deposited together in the common place. Of those three I offer one into Agni with the mind; may the Lord of Beings make her sweet for us.

sanskrit: svadvīṃ na etāṃ savitā kṛṇotu svadvīṃ na etāṃ janitā paśūnām | juhudhy agne vayunāni vidvāṃs tāṃ naḥ svādvīṃ bhūtapatiḥ kṛṇotu ||
english: May Savitṛ make her sweet for us; may the progenitor of cattle make her sweet for us. Sacrifice, O Agni, knowing all the sacred ordinances; may the Lord of Beings make her sweet for us.

sanskrit: idaṃ tṛtīyaṃ vaśinī vaśāśi mahimne tvā garbho abhy ā viveśa | uśatī tvam uśato gaccha devān satyāḥ santu yajamānasya kāmāḥ ||
english: This is the third portion of the vaśā-cow; thou art the mistress of vaśā. The embryo has entered into thee for the sake of greatness. Yearning thyself, go to the yearning gods; may the desires of the sacrificer be fulfilled.

sanskrit: iyam ambhasā vājasutastabhe gaur yasyām indro varuṇas titviṣāte | nṛmṇam anṛmṇaṃ sacata iyam āgan dhīraḥ paśur vīryam ā viveśa ||
english: This cow, steadfast with her water, sustaining vigor, in whom Indra and Varuṇa flash their brilliance — the heroic and the unheroic attend upon her; she has come here; the steadfast beast has entered into virile power.

sanskrit: vaśā sasūva sthaviraṃ vipaścitaṃ vaśā sasūva vaṣkayaṃ divispṛśan | vaśā sasūva taruṇaṃ vibhājane vaśā sasūva saṃjitaṃ dhanānām ||
english: The vaśā-cow gave birth to the steadfast wise one; the vaśā gave birth to the yearling calf touching heaven. The vaśā gave birth to the young one for the distribution; the vaśā gave birth to the conqueror of riches.

sanskrit: yat prokṣaṇam apatad barhiṣas pari dakṣiṇato vedyā indriyāvat | vaśā saṃbhūtyādhi gaur amīmet tasyāḥ pīvo abhavad varmavāsasam ||
english: The sprinkling-water that fell around the sacred grass, south of the altar, charged with vital power — the vaśā-cow lowed above it in full presence; her marrow became her armor-garment.

sanskrit: namo mahimna uta cakṣuṣe vāṃ vaśarṣabho manasā tat kṛṇomi | devām̐ apītaṃ pathibhiḥ śivebhir mā no hiṃsiṣṭaṃ harasā daivyena ||
english: Homage to your greatness and to your eye, O Vaśā and Ṛṣabha — this I do with the mind. Go together to the gods by auspicious paths; harm us not with divine wrath.

sanskrit: vaśām askandad ṛṣabhas tiṣṭhantīm adhi tantuṣu | garbhaṃ tam adya ko veda yatidhā so akalpayat ||
english: The bull mounted the vaśā-cow as she stood upon the threads of fate. Who today knows that embryo — in what manner he has disposed it?
